note: Re-judged 2026-11-20 by an independent agent after df3221e7b8, 40cf3cfaec, a29420771d, 4663a5e15e and 1dc1323b86. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "Since the SPD-I is just a part of the SPD, if a packet that is looked up in the SPD-I cannot be matched to an entry there, then the packet MUST be discarded." Producer changes read: applyConfig no longer installs the ICMP error return entries after the catch-all (the kernel maps forwarded ICMP errors, K1 bit 6) and gains warnForwardBypassAtStart, which only logs spdForwardBypassRefusals at Error and installs nothing; releaseSPD lost the matching icmpReturns.release. On the first apply installUnmatched still runs before any operator, interface or Child entry, and releaseSPD still removes the catch-all last and keeps it when warnSPDLeft reports an entry left. The two uncovered paths are unchanged (VPP CatchAllSupported answers ErrNoNodeWideSPD; the OSPF RFC 4552 manual-key entries have no final DISCARD outside the engine's window), so the gap stands.
